errors.english: If the carrier is situated on ground belonging to the boundary but has no specific purpose [note: to evade], there is no downfall.
errors.why: dgos pa med pa qualifies the mantra/medicine power: where it does not REQUIRE a carrier standing on ground inside the boundary there is no offence; where such a carrier is needed it is a sthūlātyaya; the English invents a carrier on the ground who lacks intent.

fix.find: If the carrier is situated on ground belonging to the boundary but has no specific purpose [note: to evade], there is no downfall.
fix.replace: If it does not require a carrier situated on ground belonging to the boundary, there is no downfall.

errors.english: Since there is no field of authority without such super-knowledge, there is no downfall in any case for one who possesses a mind lacking the intent to deceive.
errors.why: zhing is the Vinaya 'field', i.e. the valid object/basis of the offence (not a 'field of authority'), and yid mi ches pa is a mind of non-belief/distrust, not 'lacking the intent to deceive'.

note: Generally follows the toll-evasion discussion, but the final mantra/medicine distinction is misread and the technical 'field' is mistranslated.

errors.english: It is explained by the phrase "because of the result."
errors.why: The lemma quoted is 'because of which' (gang gis phyir), not 'because of the result'.

errors.english: Thus, if life itself is the (Pradhana), then that too becomes hollow.
errors.why: srog nyid kyis means that the potency-result is the very life/essence by which pradhāna is posited, so pradhāna too becomes hollow; it is not a conditional 'if life itself is pradhāna'.

note: A sound rendering of the refutation of the Sāṃkhya pradhāna, with two lemma/phrasing slips.

errors.english: connecting with the cognitive object
errors.why: dmigs pa here is the verb 'is observed' (upalabhyate, cf. ཉེ་བར་དམིགས་སོ below), with which 'from which cause' is construed, not 'the cognitive object'.

errors.english: Even if any particular distinction among wind and the other humors is indeed a cause
errors.why: The whole sentence from gal te through 'because it has a determinate cooperating distinction' is the anticipated objection introduced by 'or if the effect...'; the English presents its first part as the author's own statement.

errors.english: the objection is raised: "It is not so..."
errors.why: 'It is not so' (ma yin te) is the author's reply that rejects (dogs pa 'gog pa, continued on the next side) the doubt, not the raising of an objection.

note: Follows the dense humoral-causation argument tolerably, but blurs where the opponent's objection begins and ends.

errors.english: When it arises in men who wish for harm,
errors.why: The anger arises in oneself, and it is the ill-wishers (enemies) who rejoice when it does; it does not arise in them.

fix.find: When it arises in men who wish for harm,
fix.replace: When it arises, men who wish one harm

errors.english: [note: original: "gtam ngan" — here implying the loss of a worldly, aggressive reputation in favor of peace]
errors.why: The verse contrasts with the next one (whoever treats anger as an enemy gains fame like the waxing moon): the angry man is shunned and ill-repute arises for him, fading like the moon at dawn; the note rationalises a positive sense the text does not have.

fix.find: [note: original: "gtam ngan" — here implying the loss of a worldly, aggressive reputation in favor of peace]

errors.english: One will not practice the ultimate meaning.
errors.why: dam pa'i don here is the highest good/welfare (śreyas), what one should pursue, not 'the ultimate meaning' (paramārtha).

errors.english: In that anger of a king who acts wrongly,
errors.why: rgyal po is most likely a vocative ('O king, I do not dwell in that anger which makes one act wrongly'); the English makes the anger that of a wrong-acting king.

note: The Kṣānti verses are mostly rendered, but several lines shift who feels or owns the anger, and one note invents a meaning.

errors.english: The result, which is not the awareness of the aspect of the object, is indeed the cognition of the object.
errors.why: The Tibetan says the result, the awareness of the object's aspect, is itself cognition of the object, so there is no contradiction; the English inserts a negation.

fix.find: The result, which is not the awareness of the aspect of the object, is indeed the cognition of the object.
fix.replace: For the result, the awareness of the aspect of the object, is itself the cognition of the object.

errors.english: Even if the self is not the agent, it is established as such because of its influence.
errors.why: These are the last two lines of the verse (PV 3.308 akārakam api svayam / tadvaśāt tadvyavasthiteḥ): cognition, though not itself an agent, appears so because it is determined as such by virtue of that [aspect]; 'the self' is wrong and the verse lines are run into prose.

fix.find: Even if the self is not the agent, it is established as such because of its influence.
fix.replace: Though it is not itself an agent, it is so established by virtue of that [aspect].

errors.english: That which perceives its own nature
errors.why: 'dzin pa here is 'bearing/holding' (dadhānā): cognition bearing the object's form within itself, not 'perceiving its own nature'.

note: Readable treatment of pramāṇa and its result, but a negation is added at a key point and the verse on the 'as-if agent' cognition is misread.

errors.english: just as coldness is produced from fire
errors.why: The stock example of non-coexistence is cold in relation to (removed by) fire; nothing says cold is produced from fire.

fix.find: just as coldness is produced from fire
fix.replace: just as with cold in relation to fire

errors.english: because the very occurrence of a conception of an entity cuts off the continuum of the conception of non-entity
errors.why: With the instrumental བློས, it is the cognition of non-entity that cuts off the continuum of the occurring cognition of entity, by producing an incompatible cause of the nature of a vāsanā; the roles are swapped.

errors.english: By this, to avoid an absurd consequence,
errors.why: The clause describes the conception of blue as that which would entail over-extension (if any conception could cut off another), not a purpose 'to avoid' an absurdity.

note: The vāsanā-based account of incompatible conceptions is roughly conveyed, but who cuts off whom and the fire/cold example are garbled.

errors.english: being like that which is not the action of the continuum of a sacrifice
errors.why: mchod sbyin is the placeholder name Yajñadatta (paired with Devadatta, cf. 'Yajñadatta's continuum', 'the self called Yajñadatta' on the next side), not 'sacrifice/sacrificer'; the error runs through the whole side.

fix.find: being like that which is not the action of the continuum of a sacrifice
fix.replace: being like that which is not the action of Yajñadatta's continuum

errors.english: you are not subject to the fault of having an unestablished example
errors.why: The commentator says that HE ('ko bo, I') incurs no fault of an unestablished example.

fix.find: you are not subject to the fault of having an unestablished example
fix.replace: I am not subject to the fault of having an unestablished example

errors.english: Therefore, you claim that your previous inferences do not harm our position
errors.why: It is the opponents who say (zer ro) 'your earlier inferences do not harm us'; the English puts the claim in the addressee's mouth about his own inferences.

errors.english: one must ask: Is there another agent
errors.why: The dilemma (another agent or no agent; thesis lost or no example) is the dualists' objection, closed by ཞེ་ན, to which the author then replies; it is not the author's counter-question.

errors.english: [note: referring to opponent schools that maintain a rigid distinction between agent and action]
errors.why: rnam pa gnyis su smra ba are those who argue by a two-horned dilemma (as the following question shows), not a school holding an agent/action duality.

note: The Yajñadatta/Devadatta example is mistranslated as 'sacrificer' throughout, and the speakers of the debate are repeatedly swapped.

errors.english: solely out of concern for the world, he engages in external behavior
errors.why: Root verse (PV 3.219 kevalaṃ lokabuddhyaiva bāhyacintā pratanyate): solely with the world's understanding he engages in the investigation of external objects, not 'out of concern' or 'external behavior'.

fix.find: solely out of concern for the world, he engages in external behavior
fix.replace: solely by way of the world's understanding, he engages in the investigation of external objects

errors.english: Who considers that this is not of the same nature as reality?
errors.why: The root says 'it is not fit [to be known as] reality — by whom? by all who do not see the supreme'; the English garbles it into a question about who considers it different from reality.

note: The argument about non-dual reality seen only by the Buddha comes through, but the root verse on the Buddha's elephant-like feigned ignorance is misread at its key line.

errors.english: [note: original: "རྒྱུད་ཡོངས་སུ་འགྱུར་བ་" - refering to the mental continuum of the practitioner]
errors.why: The alternatives are that the application (prayoga) either produces the mantra's efficacious nature or transforms the mantra's own continuum by producing successive distinctions; the practitioner's mind is not meant.

fix.find: [note: original: "རྒྱུད་ཡོངས་སུ་འགྱུར་བ་" - refering to the mental continuum of the practitioner]
fix.replace: [note: the continuum of the mantra itself]

errors.english: This is because they are intended to be designated in that way.
errors.why: The point is that it follows from the intention of the convention-maker (the mantra's author) that results are fixed in this way; the agent is lost.

errors.english: How could those, through that very way, namely through their nature, arise from a specific natural quality?
errors.why: The Tibetan says that for nature-governed things one may rightly press the consequence 'as it arises from a particular nature, why not here too?'; the English invents a rhetorical question.

note: The critique of Mīmāṃsā mantra efficacy is followable, but a wrong note on 'continuum' and a garbled opening argument need correction.

errors.english: here there are not two ways...
errors.why: The text says the 'field' (valid object) is established here in two ways (by fact and by mind, continued on the next side); there is no negation.

fix.find: here there are not two ways...
fix.replace: here the field is established in two ways...

errors.english: [note: likely referring to the Buddha or a high authority in the Vinaya tradition]
errors.why: 'chen pos' completes མཁན་པོ་འཕགས་པ་མཽད་གལ་གྱི་བུ་ཆེན་པོས from the previous side: it was the preceptor Mahāmaudgalyāyana, whose ordaining of eighteen-year-olds occasioned the rule.

fix.find: [note: likely referring to the Buddha or a high authority in the Vinaya tradition]
fix.replace: [note: completing 'the preceptor, the noble Mahāmaudgalyāyana' from the previous side]

errors.english: The phrase "Whoever disparages these"
errors.why: smad par bya ba means 'is to be censured': those among them who are blameworthy, i.e. the remaining monks incur a duṣkṛta; nobody is disparaging anyone.

errors.english: In cases of mistaken perception or doubt, there is no efficacy here.
errors.why: The point is that perception or doubt has no power here (to invalidate the ordination of one actually twenty); the English reads as if the ordination were ineffective.

note: The age-of-twenty rules are mostly clear, but the closing sentence is negated and the Maudgalyāyana reference is mis-glossed.
